clue.text: Actor derides sleeping accommodation

parts.note: a ham is an overacting performer
to deride is to mock

explanation.surface: A performer pours scorn on the beds he has been given on tour.
explanation.definitionFit: Hammocks are slung beds of netting or canvas, used for sleeping on board ship or in gardens.

clue.text: Three articles and mother gets an object of hatred

parts.note: AN and A are the indefinite articles and THE the definite one
AN and A are the indefinite articles and THE the definite one
AN and A are the indefinite articles and THE the definite one
ma is an informal word for mother

explanation.surface: A family squabble where mother receives something everyone loathes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Three articles' supplies three separate pieces in turn: AN, A and THE.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that is anathema is intensely detested, originally a thing cursed by the church.

clue.text: Created support for church service on a large scale!

indicators.note: in a down clue the word below holds up the one above, so the second piece sits under the first

parts.note: Mass is the Catholic eucharistic service
to create is to produce

explanation.surface: A rallying cry about a congregation building up its following.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Created' looks like part of the definition, but it supplies the second piece; in a down answer the lower piece is the 'support for' the upper one.
explanation.definitionFit: Goods made in great quantities by standardised factory methods are said to be made in bulk, on a large scale.

clue.text: Little reptile found on American flower

indicators.note: in a down clue the first piece is placed on top of the second

parts.note: croc is the shortened form of crocodile, so a little version of the word
US is short for American, as in the US

explanation.surface: A tiny lizard has been discovered sitting on a bloom from the States.
explanation.definitionFit: The crocus is a small spring-flowering bulb plant with cup-shaped blooms.

clue.text: One fell from country bridge

indicators.note: the letter for one drops out of the country's name, as if falling off it

parts.note: Spain is a European country
the Roman numeral I is one

explanation.surface: Someone tumbled off a rural crossing.
explanation.definitionFit: A span is the stretch of a bridge between supports, and by extension a bridge itself.

clue.text: Agrees with fellow member — and is lying

parts.note: co- is a prefix meaning joint or fellow, as in co-worker
MP is a Member of Parliament
lies means is lying, telling untruths or reclining

explanation.surface: A colleague nods along with a fellow politician while being dishonest.
explanation.definitionFit: To comply is to go along with a request or rule, accepting it.

clue.text: A good point! Safety first means a long time

parts.note: E is east, a point of the compass

indicators.note: first picks out the opening letter of the word safety

explanation.surface: A speaker agrees enthusiastically that putting safety first pays off over years.
explanation.walkthrough: 'point' is a compass point, here E for east.
explanation.definitionFit: Ages, as in 'I waited for ages', is informal for an extended period.

clue.text: Board not up to meal of fish

parts.note: a plank is a long board of timber

indicators.note: in a down clue up means the word not is read from the bottom upwards

explanation.surface: A piece of wood falls short of being a fish supper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns NOT into TON beneath PLANK.
explanation.definitionFit: Plankton, the tiny drifting organisms of the sea, are food for many fish and whales.

clue.text: In favour of excavation, a student becomes extravagant

parts.note: pro means for or in favour of
a dig is an archaeological excavation
L is a learner, as on a learner driver's plate

explanation.surface: A keen archaeology student goes overboard spending money.
explanation.definitionFit: A prodigal person is recklessly wasteful with money, like the son in the parable.

clue.text: Plans to return unsolicited mail

indicators.note: returning means the word for junk mail is read backwards

parts.note: spam is unwanted junk email

explanation.surface: Junk mail is due to be sent back to its sender.
explanation.definitionFit: Maps are charts or diagrams, and plans of a building or area are drawn maps of it.

clue.text: You could be the support chappie

parts.note: to second a motion is to support it
a chappie is a fellow, any person

explanation.surface: A quiz asks whether the reader might be the helpful bloke.
explanation.walkthrough: 'You' is defined by example: in grammar it is the pronoun of the person addressed; 'could be the' links.
explanation.definitionFit: In grammar the pronoun used for the one being addressed belongs to the second of the three persons.

clue.text: Some politicians are true footballers

parts.note: right means true or correct
wingers play on the flanks of a football team

explanation.surface: A claim that some MPs are genuine sportsmen.
explanation.definitionFit: Right-wingers are those on the conservative side of politics.

clue.text: Formula sir Percival kept back for revenge

indicators.note: back says the held letters are then read in reverse order
kept says the letters are held inside the words formula sir Percival

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A recipe of a knight called Percival is held in reserve for vengeance.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft's 'kept back' is split: 'kept' signals the run held inside the words and 'back' turns it round, so LASIRPER becomes the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A reprisal is an act of retaliation for an injury received.

clue.text: Many have to gamble on it

parts.note: a lot means many

explanation.surface: Plenty of people feel they must have a flutter.
explanation.definitionFit: Lotto is a lottery game of chance on which people bet by choosing numbers.

clue.text: Take in seating plan, forgetting first of all

indicators.note: a plan is an arrangement, so the letters are laid out afresh
forgetting means one letter is left out of the word seating
first of picks out the opening letter of all

explanation.surface: A host must absorb the table arrangements, ignoring precedence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'first of all' is the A of all; 'forgetting' drops it from SEATING to leave SETING, which 'plan' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: To ingest food is to swallow it, taking it into the body.

clue.text: Musicians not allowed to be heard

indicators.note: says the word for prohibited is to be heard spoken rather than read

parts.note: banned means not allowed

explanation.surface: Players who have been barred from performing in public.
explanation.definitionFit: A band is a group of musicians playing together.

clue.text: One faction in plot is split

indicators.note: in says the one and the faction go inside the plot

parts.note: a bed is a garden plot
the Roman numeral I is one
a sect is a breakaway group or faction

explanation.surface: A political conspiracy is divided by a splinter group.
explanation.walkthrough: 'plot' here is a garden plot, a flower bed, not a conspiracy.
explanation.definitionFit: Bisected means cut into two parts, divided down the middle.

clue.text: Holes in places outside time

indicators.note: outside means the word for places goes round the time letter

parts.note: to put is to place

explanation.surface: Gaps in certain spots lie beyond the clock.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Holes' is a verb here: in golf one holes the ball, sinking it with a gentle stroke on the green.
explanation.definitionFit: A golfer's gentle strokes on the green aim to sink the ball, so each one that goes in holes out.

clue.text: Ascetics whom Iran puts to flight

indicators.note: to put something to flight is to scatter it, so these letters are scattered

explanation.surface: Self-denying zealots are driven away by Iran.
explanation.walkthrough: 'puts to flight' looks like one phrase, but 'puts' is fodder alongside Iran and 'to flight' signals the shuffle.
explanation.definitionFit: Puritans were strict Protestants known for austere living, and the word now means anyone rigidly self-denying.

clue.text: Spell "translate"

definitions.meaning: a spell is a stint or period of duty, as in 'my go'
to translate is to render, as in 'render the French into English'

explanation.definitionFit: A turn is a short stint at something; to turn text into another language is to translate it.

clue.text: Rebel shot a green on the outskirts of Dundee

indicators.note: shot means wrecked or damaged, so these letters are knocked out of order
the outskirts of a word are its first and last letters

explanation.surface: A golfer fires a shot onto a green on the edge of a Scottish city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shot' rearranges A GREEN; then the first and last letters of Dundee, D and E, follow. Dundee is a city in Scotland.
explanation.definitionFit: A renegade deserts a cause or faith, turning traitor or outlaw.

clue.text: Gravy run for a UFO?

parts.note: gravy is a sauce for meat
R is the cricket abbreviation for run

explanation.surface: A dash to the kitchen for gravy, joked as an alien spacecraft.
explanation.walkthrough: A UFO is popularly a flying saucer, hence the question mark.
explanation.definitionFit: Flying saucers are the classic disc-shaped alien craft of sci-fi.

clue.text: Bone tired model — no right to be compliant

indicators.note: to model is to shape, so these letters are moulded into a new form
no means the right letter is absent from the word tired

explanation.surface: An exhausted fashion model lacks moral uprightness when told to obey.
explanation.walkthrough: 'no right' removes R from TIRED, leaving TIED; 'model' rearranges BONE and TIED.
explanation.definitionFit: An obedient person does as told, readily following orders.

clue.text: Left stimulated, free of cold

indicators.note: free of says the letter for cold is removed

parts.note: excited means stimulated or aroused
C stands for cold, as on a tap

explanation.surface: A warmed-up person departed without a chill.
explanation.definitionFit: To exit is to go out, so someone who has gone has departed.

clue.text: Believe sailor's assessment?

parts.note: to credit a story is to believe it
a rating is an ordinary sailor in the navy

explanation.surface: Trust a seaman's judgement?
explanation.definitionFit: A credit rating is an evaluation of how creditworthy a borrower is.

clue.text: Executed finish with comfort

indicators.note: executed by beheading, so the word for finish loses its head

parts.note: to cease is to finish or stop

explanation.surface: A finale carried out with ease.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Executed' is not 'carried out' here but beheaded: the first letter goes.
explanation.definitionFit: Ease is a state of relaxed comfort, free from pain or effort.

clue.text: Watchers regularly taken to be experts

indicators.note: regularly says every other letter of watchers is taken

explanation.surface: Observers are routinely assumed to be specialists.
explanation.definitionFit: An ace is someone outstandingly skilled, a virtuoso.

clue.text: Feel pain regularly, but with style

indicators.note: regularly says every other letter of the words feel pain is taken

explanation.surface: Someone suffers often but carries it off with flair.
explanation.definitionFit: Elan is dash and vigour, a stylish flair.

clue.text: Settle comfortably, playing scene about prisoner

indicators.note: about means the rearranged scene goes round the prisoner
playing suggests the letters of scene are performed in a new order

parts.note: a con is a convict, a prisoner

explanation.surface: An actor relaxes into a scene about a jailbird.
explanation.walkthrough: 'playing' rearranges SCENE to ENSCE, which goes 'about' CON.
explanation.definitionFit: To ensconce yourself is to settle snugly into a safe or cosy place.

clue.text: Avoid spin before pace

indicators.note: before puts the word for spin ahead of the word for pace

parts.note: side is spin put on a ball in snooker or billiards
a step is a pace

explanation.surface: A bowler's advice: vary the spin ahead of the run-up speed.
explanation.walkthrough: In snooker and billiards, 'side' is spin applied by striking the cue ball off-centre.
explanation.definitionFit: To sidestep something is to dodge it, physically or as an issue.
